title: The Blind Spot in the Darkness
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention; Kogoro's staged second blackout and final confrontation are represented through the reactions/edges of the other participants (e.g. Yoko's incriminating rush toward the bathroom, her final confession attrs) rather than through a Kogoro node. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep170-171_the_blind_spot_in_the_darkness.json, wiki-summary-derived) correctly identified Yoko Araide as the culprit -- no discrepancy there, label.murderer_id is unchanged -- but it was otherwise thin: it omitted the entire backstory motive chain (Yoshiteru's first wife Chiaki, driven to drink by his philandering, dying in a drunk-driving accident and extracting a promise from her nursing-school classmate Yoko to protect her son Tomoaki; Yoko's later discovery of Chiaki's diary), the grandmother Mitsu's own real (if weaker) resentment-based motive against Yoshiteru over the Western bath remodel, the specific alibi mechanism (cordless handset + mobile call-waiting trick, garden route bypassing the kitchen phone), the genuinely comparative clues (body head-position vs. the 'shaving accident' story, the phone hand-switch, the chawanmushi-dish shard that innocently explains both Hikaru's and Mitsu's suspicious behavior), and the climactic staged second blackout used to trap Yoko, plus Kogoro's final off-the-record deal to spare housemaid Hikaru Yasumoto from guilt. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: If Yoshiteru had been shocked while standing to shave as the 'accident' theory required, he should have fallen with his head toward the mirror side; instead his body was slumped with his head facing the opposite way, and the razor itself was found switched off despite needing to be running for the shaving story to hold -- together these prove the death was staged, not an accident.

Yoko was holding the household phone in her left hand when Hikaru left the kitchen to reset the breaker, but was holding it in her right hand by the time the lights came back on -- only explained if she set the phone down and picked it back up while sneaking to the bathroom and back.

A shard from the chawanmushi dish Hikaru broke and hid in her room burned her arm and later cut Mitsu's foot in the same upstairs corridor -- the single object ties together both women's otherwise-suspicious behavior (Hikaru's ~30-second detour, Mitsu still being upstairs) and clears both of the murder.

A reenactment showed the breaker round trip takes only ~34 seconds once Hikaru's detour is subtracted, while the garden route between kitchen and bathroom -- which bypasses the kitchen phone entirely -- takes only ~10 seconds round trip, comfortably fitting inside the 6-7 second call-waiting gap in Yoko's 'unbroken' phone call and proving she had the opportunity despite her alibi.
